response: No, experts do not always agree on the assessment of appropriate antimicrobial prescribing. There can be variations in opinions and guidelines due to differences in interpretation of evidence, clinical context, and regional resistance patterns. However, many experts and organizations, such as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the World Health Organization (WHO), have developed guidelines and frameworks to promote appropriate antimicrobial prescribing and reduce antibiotic resistance. These guidelines often emphasize the importance of using antimicrobials judiciously, selecting the most effective and narrow-spectrum agent, and monitoring treatment outcomes to ensure optimal patient care and minimize resistance development.
